title: Sexist Agent Output Detection with the Luna Evaluator
dataSources: Luna Sexism scores written by Splunk Agent Observability on sampled traces in the Agent Stream
description: Scores agent traces for sexist content with the Splunk-hosted Luna Sexism evaluator, so biased replies are found and fed back to the prompt owner.
value: Biased replies harm users and the brand. Scoring live traffic gives the team examples to fix prompts and guardrails against.
implementation: Turn on the Luna Sexism evaluator for the Agent Stream (Configure Evaluators), set an explicit sample rate, and review flagged traces in the stream. An evaluator scores traces that are already stored and never blocks the reply. To stop or redirect a step inline, use Agent Control (UC-13.8.26).
visualization: Sexism score column in the Agent Stream trace table, with the flagged traces listed.
knownFalsePositives: Replies that discuss bias as a topic (for example HR policy questions) may be flagged; review the span text.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The agent is already instrumented as described in UC-13.8.1: every request is a trace with at least one agent span, LLM spans carry `model`, token counts and the `tools` schemas, and tool spans carry `name`, `duration_ns` and `tool_call_id`.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Evaluators are defined for the organization and turned on per Agent Stream, in the console (Configure Evaluators) or with `enable_evaluators`. That SDK call replaces the stream's set: anything left out is turned off. Evaluators run after the trace is stored, on a sample. A 10% rate stores every trace and scores one in ten, and a sampled trace is scored by every enabled evaluator. There is no documented default sample rate, so set it explicitly. Luna evaluators are Splunk-hosted small models and need no customer model key. On SaaS, Luna is limited to Prompt Injection, Toxicity, Sexism, PII and Context Adherence.

Step 3 — Validate

Send a test request that should be flagged and one that should not, to a test stream at a 100% sample rate, and confirm the scores. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add an alert on the score from the stream's Alerts tab if the team needs to be notified (see UC-13.8.25 for the pattern). An alert on an evaluator only sees sampled traces.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Unexpected flags: read the rationale and the span output together before changing the prompt.
grandmaExplanation: A reviewer reads the assistant's replies afterwards and flags any that treat people unfairly because of their sex.
